content:
According to a new report from Bloomberg, Apple is less than two weeks away from unveiling a brand-new smart display. The report also reveals further design details of Apple's long-awaited smart home hub.

Bloomberg reports that the home hub will feature a 6-inch square display, with an overall design reminiscent of the classic iMac G4—which featured a hemispherical base supporting the display via a metal arm.

According to Mark Gurman, the device is "roughly the thickness of an iPhone," with bezels of about a quarter inch in black, similar to older iPads. The body features rounded corners with "no sharp edges."

Here are more design details from the report:

  • The body uses Apple's "standard gray aluminum enclosure," with a "rubber coating" on the bottom to keep it securely placed on a table surface.
  • It has a USB-C port for power, with no built-in battery, meaning it must be plugged in at all times to operate.
  • The base is a "circular metal design with multiple rings of perforated speaker holes."
  • The display connects to the base via a "polished metal arm."
  • Users can adjust the tilt angle of the display forward or backward.
  • There are no volume or power buttons on the device.
  • The front features a single FaceTime camera, with no rear camera.

Bloomberg also mentions another version of the home hub designed to be "wall-mountable." This version is also powered by USB-C, with a "thin square base housing speakers and a microphone" beneath the display. The base reportedly "sits flush against the wall, below the screen."

For the full report, head over to Bloomberg. What are your thoughts on Apple's home hub product? Planning to pick up one or several? Feel free to share your views in the comments section.
